Is that a snake in the dark, or just a rope?

Kevin Trudeau describes walking into a pitch-black basement and seeing a snake coiled in the corner. You scream. Then someone turns on the light, and it was only a rope.

He says that is what knowledge does. When a person walks around half asleep, they see threats that are not there. Once you see what is really in front of you, the fear goes away.

What is one fear in your life that might just be a rope?

#ad #mindset #fear #kevintrudeau

Upside down in a Corvette, in the rain, with no phone. Kevin Trudeau laughed.

In 1984 he and his friend Dan were headed out in Orlando when the car flipped. They got out safely, soaked, with no cars passing and no cell phones.

Dan was upset. Kevin told him that someday they would look back and laugh, so why wait? Whether he was happy or sad, the situation would stay the same, so he chose to enjoy the moment.

When something goes wrong, do you choose your mood or let it choose for you?

#ad #happiness #mindset #kevintrudeau

Look around any airport gate. Almost everyone is staring at a screen.

Kevin Trudeau says we are being programmed to constantly be doing and thinking. He calls the cell phone a great tool and also a great trap, because it keeps so many people hooked on the device.

He describes sitting at the airport, looking around, and not finding a single person who was not on a phone, except him.

When did you last sit for a while with no screen at all?

#ad #habits #mindset #kevintrudeau

Are you a snipe? Zig Ziglar had a name for it.

Kevin Trudeau recalls his friend Zig Ziglar, author of See You at the Top. Zig warned him to beware of becoming a snipe, which stands for susceptible to the negative influence of other people.

Kevin says most people today are more susceptible to it than ever before in his memory. The people around you shape your thinking, whether you notice it or not.

Who influences your thinking the most?
